title: The role of C5a in Rheumatoid and Psoriatic Arthritis in comparison with Osteoarthritis - Profiling of Synovial and Systemic Biomarkers
author: Else Marie Bartels

steps_raw.instruction: Protocol The role of C5a in Rheumatoid and Psoriatic Arthritis in comparison with Osteoarthritis - Profiling of Synovial and Systemic Biomarkers Lars Hornum1, Anker Jon Hansen1, Ditte Tornehave1, Marianne Scheel Fjording1, Paula Colmenero3, Inger Falbe Wätjen2, Niels Henrik Søe Nielsen4, Henning Bliddal2,5, Else Marie Bartels2 1Novo Nordisk A/S, Måløv, Denmark 2The Parker Institute, Copenhagen University Hospital, Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg, Frederiksberg, Denmark 3Radcliffe Department of Medicine, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK 4Hand Section, Department of Orthopaedics, Herlev and Gentofte Hospital, Gentofte, Denmark 5Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark

Abstract Complement activation correlates to rheumatoid arthritis disease activity, and increased amounts of the complement split product C5a is observed in synovial fluids from rheumatoid arthritis patients. Blockade of C5a or its receptor (C5aR) is efficacious in several arthritis models. The aim of this study is to investigate the role of C5a and C5aR in human rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis – both with respect to expression and function. Synovial fluid, blood and synovial samples will be obtained from rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and osteoarthritis patients as a less inflammatory arthritis type, and blood from healthy subjects. Cells infiltrating synovial tissue will analysed by immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry. SF and blood will be analysed for biomarkers by flow cytometry or ELISA. The effect of a blocking anti-human C5aR mAb on leukocyte migration will be determined using a Boyden chamber. Appropriate statistical tests will be applied for comparisons.

Introduction The introduction of biological agents for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis has significantly changed the course of this disabling disease. Despite this improvement, only a fraction of the patients obtains an adequate clinical response to TNF- antagonists.1 Moreover, the risk of cardiovascular disease is significantly elevated in patients with RA, and it remains to be seen if new biological agents can block the atherogenic process and hence improve cardiovascular co-mobidity.27 The role of complement in the pathogenesis of RA has historically been described in both human and animal studies, and C5a has been hypothesised to play a pivotal role in the disease process.7 Elevated levels of C5a have been observed in synovial fluid samples and both chondrocytes and synovial mast cells from RA patients have been shown to express the C5a receptor.8-11 In support, C5a-stimulated human neutrophils are a well-known source of various matrix metalloproteinases involved in cartilage and extracellular matrix turnover.21-23 Moreover, C5a stimulates monocyte production of IL-8 which in RA has been shown to further activate neutrophil production of matrix metalloproteinases.24,25 Interestingly, both the cytokine IL-8 and Matrix Metalloprotease 3 (MMP3) has recently been shown to predict clinical outcome of infliximab and methotrexate therapy.26 Despite these studies, a direct correlation between C5a activity and arthritic disease activity remains to be established in humans. A special group is the Psoriatic arthritis patients (PSA). In some way this group shows similar symptoms and biological markers as RA, but in others ways this group diverges from RA; among others, PSA shows a site-specific extra-capsular region of attack in a certain proportion of the cases32. In various joints like PIP and knee, RA and PSA have to be differentiated from osteoarthritis (OA) which may present itself with the same clinical signs and symptoms. The diseases may be separated by inflammatory markers. However, some common markers of joint inflammation cannot differ between the diseases33. Complement activation, indicated by the elevation of C5a, has been suggested associated with increased cardiovascular risk in patients with advanced atherosclerosis28, 29. Apart from being a strong chemotactic factor for atherogenic inflammatory subsets, C5a stimulates secretion of important inflammatory mediators such as TNF- as well as the thrombolytic inhibitor PAI-1 from human mononuclear cells.30,31 Importantly, the C5a-mediated effects on atherosclerotic plaque macrophages are independent of TNF- indicating a more upstream pathogenic role for C5a, when compared to TNF- in atherosclerosis.31 In addition, C5a induces the expression of endothelial adhesion molecules such as P-selectin15 . Both TNF- , PAI-1, and P-selectin are important risk factors for cardiovascular disease. We hypothesize that the suggested upstream atherogenic role for C5a, when compared to TNF- may be important in C5aR versus TNF- -targeted prevention of cardiovascular co-morbidity in RA. In order to tailor treatment towards patients who are most likely to benefit from targeted biological treatment, both pharmaco-genomic and -metabonomic studies have been initiated.2 Several smaller studies point towards that genomic and metabonomic profiling are feasible tools in separating responders from non-responders (Lauridsen et al., unpublished results).3,4 In addition, important understanding of mechanism of action of novel compounds in clinical testing may be unravelled and further exploited to tailor treatment towards specific patient populations.5 In addition, a histological approach has shown to be predictive of long-term response to various anti-rheumatic agents, including biological agents.6 However, this technique requires strict adherence to specific protocols for synovial tissue sampling that is difficult to

adapt in routine clinical practice and large multi-centre clinical trials. Hence, novel biomarkers of disease activity linked to biological mechanism of action of novel compounds are needed in order to guide future treatment and dosing in rheumatoid arthritis. Aims The aim of the study is to evaluate the role of C5a in rheumatoid and psoriatic arthritis in comparison with osteoarthritis, and to identify biomarkers that can be used for monitoring a successful blockade of C5a signalling in the clinic. A secondary aim is to evaluate the role of the TL1A/DR3 ligand/receptor pair in the same setting. Objectives Primary Objective To evaluate the role of C5a in rheumatoid and psoriatic arthritis (RA and PsA) when compared to osteoarthritis (OA). Secondary Objective To identify C5a regulated genes, proteins and metabolites that can be utilized as biomarkers for successful C5aR blockade in the clinic. Hypotheses 1. C5a is elevated in SF and plasma in RA and/or PsA patients relative to OA 2. C5a levels correlate to disease activity as defined by peripheral blood CRP-level or inflammatory cytokine levels in SF (IL-6 and TNFα)1 3. C5a levels correlate to presence/titer of autoantibodies in plasma (RF and ACPA) 4. C5a levels in SF and plasma correlate 5. C5aR density is inversely correlated to disease activity and/or to C5a levels in SF 6. C5aR blockade will significantly inhibit chemotaxis of leukocytes (specifically DCs) Materials and Methods Participants 1 Also valid for PSA: Gisondo and Girolomoni, 2009; Vandooren et al, 2009; Canete et al, 2009

A total of 30 patients with active RA, 10 patients with active PSA, and 10 patients with active OA will be included in the study. 30 healthy age- and sex-matched women and men will have blood taken for comparison with the patient groups. criteria).  Active arthritis with joint swelling and tenderness  Patients must be fastening from midnight prior to sampling, only water intake is allowed. Exclusion criteria patients  An alcohol consumption of more than an amount equivalent to 1 unit of alcohol 12 hours or less prior to sampling is not allowed  Active medical treatment for other chronic diseases than rheumatoid arthritis Prior to study enrolment, patients must not be in active treatment with any of the following medications: Glucocorticoid unless given in stable doses equivalent to ≤ 10 mg of prednisone orally /day the preceding month Intra-articular, i.m. or i.v. corticosteroids within the last month Cyclosporine Azathioprine Penicillamine Etanercept Infliximab Abatacept Efalizumab Alefacept Adalimumab

Clinical and Biochemical Information For each patient biochemical test for HDL, LDL, triglyceride concentration, total cholesterol, serum rheumatic factor, anti-CCP, CRP, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and urine creatinine must be available. In addition information regarding smoking habits and intake of over-the-counter drugs must be made available through a questionnaire. Age, duration of disease and gender must also be available. Flow cytometric Analyses Flow cytometric analyses of synovial fluid cells or cells from whole blood will be performed using the BD Biosciences FACSArray instrument, which measures emitted fluorescence light in four channels only, not five channels. This makes it necessary to aliquot cells and use fluorochrome conjugated antibodies in the way stated below. A labelling of the predominant cell types in synovial fluid, namely macrophage-like synoviocytes (type A synoviocytes) and fibroblast-like synoviocytes (type B synoviocytes) is added: FACS protocol 1. From each patient 2 x 3 FACS staining tubes (Axygen MCT-150-L-C) are set up (3 from SF and 3 from blood). 2. To 300 µl EDTA-anticoagulated whole blood are added 30 µl of a 100 µg/ml solution of human IgG (Sigma I-4506) in Staining Buffer (PBS pH 7.40 with 0.2% human serum albumin (Sigma A-1653) and 0.09% w/v sodium azide). Mixing, then standing at room temperature for 15 minutes.

Immunohistochemistry Human tissue samples from RA, PsA and OA, as well as from non-inflammatory controls will be studied. Sectioning Fixed paraffin embedded cell and tissue sections are cut at a nominal thickness of 3 μm, mounted on Superfrost®Plus microscope slides, and stored at -20°C until further processing. Immunostaining for microscopy

The sections will be deparaffinised in xylene and rehydrated in decreasing concentrations of alcohols. Antigen retrieval will be performed in Tris-EGTA buffer (10mM; 0.5 mM), pH 9.0 in a microwave oven for 15 min. Endogenous peroxidase activity is blocked with 3% H2O2. Endogenous biotin is blocked by incubation with Avidin and Biotin blocking solutions for 10 min, according to the manufacturer. Non-specific binding is blocked by incubation with TBS containing 3% skimmed milk, 7% donkey serum, 3% human serum, and 3.2 mg/ml Poly-L-Lysine (PLL) for 30 min. The primary and secondary antibodies will be diluted in a Tris buffer containing 0.5% skimmed milk, 7% donkey, 3% human sera, and incubation is performed overnight at 4°C (primary antibody), and 60 min at room temperature (secondary antibody). The first amplification step will be performed by incubation with Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit, diluted in 0.1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 7,5) containing 0.5% Du Pont Blocking Reagent (TNB) for 30 min, followed by a second amplification step with incubation in biotinylated Tyramide for 6 min. The final amplification is performed by an additional incubation with the Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit, diluted as previously described for 30 min. The chromogenic reaction is achieved with diaminobenzidin. Nuclei will be counterstained with haematoxylin and the sections be rehydrated, cleared in xylene and mounted with Eukitt. Evaluation of the slides will be performed blinded to the observer. Double-immunofluorescence The immunohistochemical demonstration of the C5aR will be performed as described above. Upon the second amplification with biotinylated Tyramide for 3 min sections are incubated with the Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit, diluted as previously described for 30 min. The final amplification is performed by incubation with Alexa-594 conjugated Tyramide diluted according to manufacturer for 6 min. Sections are then subjected to second rounds of microwave oven treatment in Tris-EGTA buffer (10mM; 0.5 mM), pH 9.0 for 10 min, blocking of endogenous peroxidase activity with 3% H2O2, and endogenous biotin by incubation with Avidin and Biotin blocking solutions for 10 min, respectively, according to the manufacturer. Additional blocking of non-specific binding is performed by incubation with TBS containing 3% skimmed milk, 7% donkey serum, and 3% human serum for 30 min. The second primary and secondary antibodies are diluted in a Tris buffer containing 0.5% skimmed milk, 7% donkey and 3% human sera, and incubation is performed overnight at 4°C, and 60 min at room temperature, respectively. The final amplifications are performed by an additional incubation with the Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit, diluted as previously described for 30 min, and incubation with Alexa-488 conjugated Tyramide. Nuclei will be counterstained with Hoechst for 15 min, and the sections be mounted in fluorescence mounting media (Dako). Microscopic analyses Sections are evaluated by virtual microscopy using either a Hamamatsu NanoZoomer (Hamamatsu Denmark, Ballerup, Denmark), or a FV10i Laser scanning microscope (Olympus Denmark A/S; Ballerup, Denmark), and an Olympus BX51 reflected fluorescence system microscope equipped with selective AMCA, FITC and Texas-Red filters, and a DP70 digital camera (Olympus Denmark A/S; Ballerup, Denmark).

Flow cytometry analysis of RA synovial tissue cells Tissue RA synovial membranes will obtained from patients undergoing joint replacement surgery or synovectomy. Cell Preparation for flow cytometry from synovial tissue Single-cell suspensions of RA synovial tissue biopsies will be prepared by mechanical disruption followed by enzymatic digestion for 1-2 h using Liberase TL (Roche, Welwyn Garden City, UK) and DNAse (Sigma-Aldrich Ltd, Dorset, UK). After passing the cells through a nylon mesh to exclude debris, cells are washed and resuspended in RPMI-1640 medium (containing 10% (v/v) FBS) at a density of 1x106 cells/ml. For FACS analysis, dead cells are excluded with Live/Dead Fixable Aqua Dead Cell Stain (Life Technologies, Waltham, MA, USA). After gating on viable CD45+ cells within the monocytic gate, CD14 vs. CD15 staining was used to identify macrophages and infiltrating neutrophils. The following anti-human monoclonal antibodies from BD Biosciences (San Jose, CA, USA) will be used: CD14-APC (clone M5E2), CD15-PECy7 (clone HI98), CD45-
PerCP (clone TU116). Anti-human C5aR/CD88-PE (clone S5/1, Biolegend, London, UK) and mIgG2a-PE (clone MOPC-173, Biolegend, London, UK) will be used to assess C5aR expression. To block non-specific Fc receptor-mediated antibody binding, FcR Blocking reagent (Miltenyi Biotec, Lund, Sweden) is used prior to antibody staining. Stained cells are fixed in Fixation Buffer (BD Biosciences, San Jose, CA, USA). Samples will be acquired in a BD Fortessa flow cytometer (BD Biosciences, San Jose, CA, USA) and analyzed using FlowJo software (Tree Star, Ashland, OR, USA). Ethics Ethics Committee for London Riverside and for the Capital Region of Denmark and the Danish Data Protection Agency will be sought for permissions to carry out the study and handle the data. Statistics Student’s t-test will be used for group comparisons, Spearman’s Rank correlation test for correlations tests. To correct for multiple comparisons, Bonferoni correction will be applied.
